### ProtocolCorrection

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: A correction, for PUT /api/moderation/protocols/{id} . machineNo and protocolType are sent back unchanged and checked rather than applied — the backend answers 400 PROTOCOL\_IDENTITY\_LOCKED if either differs. They are in the shape because the form submits every field it shows, and the edit dialog shows both, read-only: a protocol's machine is its provenance, not its content (ADR-006 revision). Words can be fixed, identity cannot.

Properties:
- `comment: string` — Why. Required — the backend refuses a blank one, and so does the dialog.
- `content: string`
- `errorCode: string`
- `machineNo: string`
- `protocolType: string`
- `title: string`

### ProtocolDocument

File: `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`

Description: A protocol as the viewer will render it. kind is the honest half: 'parsed' means the structure below was recognised, 'raw' means it was not and the viewer must fall back to the file as it stands. The corpus ships a documented quality mix (90 well-written, 45 terse, 15 messy) and one uploaded protocol already has no banner, no header block and no title at all — so "the parser did not recognise this" is a normal outcome to be rendered, not an error to be reported.

Properties:
- `kind: "parsed" | "raw"`
- `raw: string`
- `segments: {}`

### ProtocolFilter

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: What the corpus list is narrowed to. Every field is a form value, so "" means "not filled in". The machine is not optional in practice: the backend refuses a title or date filter without one (400 MACHINE\_REQUIRED\_FOR\_FILTER ), because across ten machines a title fragment on its own answers with rows the reviewer was not looking at. The view enforces the same rule by disabling the other fields, so the 400 is a backstop rather than something a user can reach.

Properties:
- `approvalState: ApprovalState | string` — The approval queue, and the one filter that is NOT subject to the machine-first rule. That rule exists because a title fragment across ten machines answers with rows the reviewer was not looking at. "Everything still waiting for review" is the opposite: a queue is only useful whole, and it is the first question an administrator asks after signing in. The backend agrees — it applies approvalState without requiring machineNo .
- `from: string` — ISO yyyy-MM-dd , as an \<input type="date"\> produces it.
- `machineNo: string`
- `titleContains: string`
- `to: string`

### ProtocolHistory

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: A protocol's recent history, from GET /api/moderation/protocols/{id}/history . events is capped SERVER-side; total is how many exist. The pair is what lets the viewer say that older entries exist rather than presenting the newest three as though they were everything. An empty list is a true answer, not a missing one. The 150 seeded protocols were approved by the V5 migration itself — system:corpus-seed , no human act — so they have no ledger rows and never will. The viewer falls back to the approval columns on the protocol for exactly that case.

Properties:
- `events: {}`
- `limit: number` — The server-side cap, sent so no screen hard-codes a number the backend is free to change.
- `total: number`

### ProtocolPage

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: One page of the corpus. total is what turns "Weiter" into "page 3 of 16".

Properties:
- `items: {}`
- `page: number`
- `size: number`
- `total: number`

### QueryAnswer

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: The answer, from POST /api/query . answer already carries its inline \[P1\] markers and its claims are already validated against what was retrieved. The client renders it; it does not re-parse, reorder or second-guess it.

Properties:
- `answer: string`
- `citations: {}`
- `claims: {}`
- `language: string` — The language the backend pinned the answer to — independent of the UI language.
- `mode: AnswerMode`

### RuntimeConfig

File: `src/app/core/config/runtime-config.ts`

Description: Configuration the application reads at runtime rather than at build time. The container image is built once by CI and deployed to every environment, so it cannot contain a hostname. The deployment supplies /config.json instead — a bind mount in production, a static file under public/ in development — and the values compiled into environment.ts are the fallback when that file is missing or unreadable.

Properties:
- `apiBaseUrl: string` — Backend base URL. Same-origin in every environment, so a relative path.
- `keycloakClientId: string` — Public client id from the versioned realm export.
- `keycloakIssuer: string` — Keycloak realm base URL — the OIDC issuer.

### SearchExample

File: `src/app/core/i18n/dictionary.ts`

Description: A worked pair for the search help panel: a question that retrieves well, and the one people actually type first. The weak half is not a strawman — it is what a single word does to a semantic search, and showing it beside its fix teaches the rule faster than the rule does.

Properties:
- `good: string`
- `weak: string`

### SimilarityReport

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: What the approver is shown before they decide. Information, never a gate. No field here is capable of refusing an approval and no code path treats it as though it were: the four E-47 protocols on PR-03 are four different root causes behind one fault code, every one of them legitimate, and a threshold sensitive enough to catch a genuine duplicate would report them as copies of each other.

Properties:
- `allIds: {}` — Every id above the threshold. The ledger's field; the interface reads candidates .
- `candidates: {}` — The most similar first, at most three.
- `comparable: boolean` — False when the protocol has no vectors yet — filed seconds ago, or its indexing failed. A different fact from "nothing similar", and typed separately so the two cannot arrive as the same empty list. The view treats both as "no dialog", because neither is something an approver can act on; the distinction exists so the API does not have to lie.
- `threshold: number` — The threshold in force, sent by the backend so no screen hard-codes a configurable number.
- `total: number` — How many cleared the threshold in all — so a long tail is visible rather than cut silently.

### SimilarProtocol

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: A protocol on the same machine that says close to what the one being approved says, from GET /api/moderation/protocols/{id}/similar . approval is the candidate's OWN state, and it is the reason a card is worth reading rather than a detail on it: "nearly the same as a protocol an administrator already vouched for" is a merge-or-reject question, while "nearly the same as one nobody has reviewed" may simply be two people describing one fault from different angles — which this corpus wants both of.

Properties:
- `approval: Approval`
- `id: string`
- `incidentDate: string` — The day of the incident, not of the upload — what a duplicate would duplicate.
- `similarity: number` — Cosine similarity of the two protocols' chunk centroids, 0..1. Shown as a percentage.
- `title: string`
- `uploadedAt: string`
- `uploadedBy: string`

### SourceFocus

File: `src/app/features/search/search-sources.ts`

Description: One request to reveal a source, as an object rather than an id. The identity is the point: two clicks on the same marker are two events, and a signal holding a bare string would only notify on the first.

Properties:
- `protocolId: string`

### UploadAccepted

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: What POST /api/protocols answers with its 202.

Properties:
- `id: string`
- `message: string`
- `status: string`

### UploadStatus

File: `src/app/core/api/api.types.ts`

Description: One of the caller's uploads, from GET /api/protocols/mine .

Properties:
- `createdAt: string`
- `failureReason: string | null` — Why it failed; null unless FAILED.
- `id: string`
- `indexedAt: string | null`
- `machineNo: string`
- `status: "RECEIVED" | "INDEXED" | "FAILED"`
- `title: string`

## Public functions

- `archived(overrides: Partial = {}): ArchivedProtocol`
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `archivePage(items, total: unknown = items.length, index: number = 0, cap: number = 50): DeletedProtocolPage`
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `buildAuthConfig(config: RuntimeConfig): AuthConfig` — Builds the OIDC client configuration for the Keycloak realm maintenance (ADR-003). A function rather than a constant because the issuer is only known once /config.json has been read — the image is environment-agnostic, so nothing about the deployment can be decided at module-evaluation time. Authorization Code Flow with PKCE: the browser is a public client that cannot keep a secret, so PKCE replaces the client secret.
  Defined in `src/app/core/auth/auth.config.ts`
- `classify(error): ApiFailure` — Maps a failed request to the message the user should read. The NFR-7 guards reach the surface here, and they mean different things to a person: 429 is "you, in a moment", a spent daily budget is "everyone, tomorrow", and an unreachable provider is "try again shortly". One text for all three would make a rate limit look like an outage. The backend sends both budget exhaustion and provider trouble as 503 and distinguishes them with a reason code in the body. The code is read rather than the message, so rewording the English sentence on the server does not silently change what the German UI says.
  Defined in `src/app/core/api/maintenance-api.service.ts`
- `click(fixture: ComponentFixture, testId: string): Promise<void>` — Clicks by test id and lets the resulting change detection settle.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `filenameOf(contentDisposition): string` — The readable filename the backend put in Content-Disposition , for the download action.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `find(fixture: ComponentFixture, testId: string): HTMLElement | null` — The element carrying a test id, or null when the view does not render it.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `get(fixture: ComponentFixture, testId: string): HTMLElement` — The element carrying a test id. Throws when it is absent, so a typo fails as a typo.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `homePath(realmRoles): string` — Where a role belongs when it has nowhere else to be: after login, and after being turned away from a route it may not have. The admin's home is moderation, and that is a defect fix rather than a preference. Their home was /search , the search view's first call is GET /api/machines , and until this PR that endpoint refused a role with no shop-floor function — so an administrator's first screen was an error message. Search is not a view an admin can use at all: they may not ask questions, by decision.
  Defined in `src/app/core/auth/role.guard.ts`
- `initialLanguage(): UiLanguage` — A remembered choice wins; otherwise the browser decides. German is the fallback rather than English because the plant, the corpus and the demo users are German — the setting this models is a German shop floor, and a visitor whose browser says nothing useful is better served by the language the protocols are written in.
  Defined in `src/app/core/i18n/i18n.service.ts`
- `noSimilar(http: HttpTestingController, id: string = 'p-1'): void` — Answers the duplicate check that every approval makes first, with nothing similar. The empty answer is the ordinary case — no dialog, one click — so a spec that is not about duplicate detection only needs it flushed and out of the way.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `openArchive(fixture: ComponentFixture, http: HttpTestingController, first: DeletedProtocolPage = archivePage([archived()])): Promise<void>` — Switches to the archive tab and answers the page it loads on arrival.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `openEdit(fixture: ComponentFixture, http: HttpTestingController, roles: Roles, text: string = 'Anzugsmoment 90 Nm'): Promise<void>` — Opens the correction dialog on the first row and answers the document fetch it makes. AS THE SCHICHTLEITER, because correcting has been theirs since 2026-08-13 and the administrator has no Bearbeiten button at all. The role is set here so a consuming test can go on saying what the dialog does rather than repeating who may open it.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `openViewer(fixture: ComponentFixture, http: HttpTestingController, options = {}): Promise<void>` — Opens the read-only viewer on a row and answers BOTH calls it makes. The history call is easy to forget and impossible to ignore: an unanswered request fails \`verify()\` in the teardown, which is the mechanism that makes "nothing else was sent" an assertion rather than a hope.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `page(items, total: unknown = items.length, index: number = 0): ProtocolPage`
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `parseProtocol(text: string): ProtocolDocument` — Parses a protocol file into typed segments, and never throws. The structure is stable across the corpus but not guaranteed: it is plain text written by people, and the messy end of the quality mix omits whichever part it feels like. So every step is optional. A file with only sections parses; a file with only a header block parses; a file that matches nothing at all comes back as 'raw' and the viewer shows it preformatted. What must never happen is a blank dialog — the reader clicked a citation and is entitled to the evidence behind it, in whatever shape it exists.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `protocol(overrides: Partial = {}): ModeratedProtocol`
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `readMeta(lines, from: number): MetaRow[]` — The run of Key: Value lines starting at from , which ends at the first line that is not one.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `readSections(lines, from: number): ProtocolSegment[]` — Everything from from on, grouped under the section labels it contains. Text appearing before the first label is kept under an empty heading rather than dropped: an unlabelled paragraph is still what the technician wrote, and losing it would make the viewer a less complete record than the file.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `reasonOf(error: HttpErrorResponse): string | null` — The body is JSON in practice and untyped in principle; a missing code is simply not a match.
  Defined in `src/app/core/api/maintenance-api.service.ts`
- `renderModeration(http: HttpTestingController, first: ProtocolPage = page([protocol()])): Promise<ComponentFixture<Moderation>>` — Creates the component and answers the two calls its constructor makes. Both are answered here because neither is what any consuming spec is about: a test that had to flush the machine list before it could click a tab would be describing the constructor.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `roleGuard(...allowed): CanActivateFn` — Keeps a route out of the hands of roles that have no business on it. Like authGuard, this is convenience and not security: the upload endpoint refuses anyone but a Schichtleiter server-side, which is the only place the decision counts (NFR-3). What this buys is that an operator following a bookmarked /upload link gets their own view rather than a form that produces a 403 after they have chosen a file — and that an admin who types /search gets the view they can use rather than a machine picker that cannot be filled. Turned-away callers land on homePath rather than on a hard-coded /search , which is what makes one guard serve both directions: /upload is refused to an admin and /search is refused to an admin, and both send them to moderation.
  Defined in `src/app/core/auth/role.guard.ts`
- `setUpModeration(roles = ['admin']): Promise<ModerationHarness>` — Configures the TestBed and returns the handles a spec needs. Call from \`beforeEach\`. The language is pinned to German because the interface under test is German and an unpinned one would read whatever localStorage held from the previous file.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `skipBanner(lines): number` — Steps over the banner line and its ===== rule, if the file has them.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `skipBlank(lines, from: number): number`
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `sourceCardId(citation: Citation): string` — Stable per protocol, so a citation marker can find its card without an index that shifts.
  Defined in `src/app/features/search/search-sources.ts`
- `storedChoice(): ThemeChoice` — The stored override, or system when there is none. Anything unrecognised counts as no override rather than as an error: the key is in localStorage where a user or an old build could have left anything, and the worst outcome of a bad value should be the default theme. That covers the migration for free — the three-state control wrote the literal "system" , which is now simply an unrecognised value and therefore means "no override", exactly what it meant before.
  Defined in `src/app/core/theme/theme.service.ts`
- `storedScale(): FontScale` — Anything unrecognised is the default rather than an error — the key lives in localStorage.
  Defined in `src/app/core/theme/font-scale.service.ts`
- `tearDownModeration(http: HttpTestingController): void` — Exit clear: the only cleanup the next file inherits. Call from afterEach .
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `toSegments(answer: string, citations): AnswerSegment[]` — Splits an answer into prose and \[Pn\] markers. A marker whose label is not among the citations is left as plain text rather than dropped or linked: the backend already removed every claim citing a source it did not retrieve, so if one still appears here it belongs to prose and inventing a link for it would be the client asserting something the server did not.
  Defined in `src/app/features/search/search-answer.ts`
- `type(fixture: ComponentFixture, testId: string, value: string): Promise<void>` — Fills a field the way a user does — through the event Angular's forms binding listens for — so the template's own listener runs rather than a signal being set behind it.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.fixtures.ts`
- `typedProtocolFilename(machineNo: string, at: Date): string` — The filename a typed protocol is stored and later downloaded under: \<machineNo\>-\<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss\>-eingabe.txt . ASCII only, and not for tidiness: this name travels to the volume and comes back in Content-Disposition when the viewer offers the download, and every layer in between has its own opinion about non-ASCII filenames. The machine number is the useful half — a Schichtleiter scanning the uploads list wants to see which press it was — and the timestamp to the second is what keeps two protocols typed in the same shift apart. Local time rather than UTC, deliberately: the name is read by the person who typed it, and 22:14 means their shift, not a timezone conversion.
  Defined in `src/app/features/upload/upload.ts`

## Public type aliases

- `type AnswerMode = "A" | "B"` — NFR-2's two answer modes.
- `type ApiFailure = "rateLimited" | "budgetExhausted" | "unavailable" | "tooLarge" | "rejectedContent" | "identityLocked" | "archived" | "forbidden" | "notFound" | "generic"` — The statuses the UI has a specific sentence for. Everything else collapses to a generic message, deliberately: inventing a distinct wording per status code produces a wall of text nobody maintains, and the three below are the ones a user can actually act on — wait a moment, come back tomorrow, or ask someone for a role.
- `type ApprovalState = "APPROVED" | "UNAPPROVED"` — The two states approval can be in. A closed set on the wire, matching the schema's constraint.
- `type DocumentSource = "citation" | "moderation" | "archive"` — Which endpoint a viewer reads its document from. Three paths for the same file, and they differ in exactly one thing: who may take them, and what they are allowed to serve. citation is the shop-floor path; moderation is the admin's view of the live corpus; archive is the only door back to a protocol that was removed — the other two answer 404 for it. A single endpoint with a flag would put that distinction in a parameter instead of in the URL, where the authorisation rule can be read.
- `type FontScale = "normal" | "lg" | "xl"` — The three steps offered. normal is the absence of an attribute, not a value of it.
- `type HealthState = "unknown" | "up" | "down"` — Neutral until the first answer arrives; a guess before then would be a lie either way.
- `type InputMode = "file" | "text"` — How the protocol got into the form: picked as a file, or typed here.
- `type KnownRole = typeof KNOWN_ROLES['number']`
- `type ModerationAction = "EDIT" | "DELETE" | "APPROVE" | "UNAPPROVE"` — The vocabulary the moderation ledger can spell, matching the schema's own check constraint. UNAPPROVE rather than WITHDRAW — the verb the database has recorded since #53. The interface says "Freigabe zurückgezogen"; renaming the stored value would be a data migration and a sweep of three services to change a word no user reads.
- `type ProtocolSegment = literal type | literal type | literal type` — One piece of a parsed protocol. Typed segments, exactly like the answer renderer's: the template switches on kind and binds text, so there is no path from a protocol file into innerHTML . The corpus is synthetic today and a Schichtleiter can upload arbitrary text tomorrow, which makes this the same rule and not merely the same style.
- `type ResolvedTheme = "light" | "dark"` — What is actually on screen once system has been resolved against the operating system.
- `type Roles = WritableSignal<string[]>` — The roles the signed-in reader holds. Flipped per test, because the buttons depend on them.
- `type ThemeChoice = "light" | "dark" | "system"` — What the user chose, which is not the same as what is painted. system is the absence of a choice rather than a third button. The control offers light and dark; until one of them is pressed the application silently follows the operating system, which is what a first visit should do without spending a third of a segmented control saying so.
- `type UiLanguage = "de" | "en"` — The two languages the interface is offered in (DECISIONS.txt: bilingual DE/EN).

- `META_LINE: unknown = /^([^:]{1,40}):[ \t]+(\S.*)$/` — A Key: Value header line. The key is short and colon-free; the value is whatever follows.

- `PAGE_SIZE: number = 5` — Rows per page. Five, not ten: on a tablet held upright ten rows push the pager below the fold, so the control that says there is more is only reachable by scrolling past everything it is offering. Five rows and a pager both fit.
  Defined in `src/app/features/moderation/moderation.ts`
- `PAGE_SIZE: number = 5` — Rows per page in "Meine Uploads" — the same five the two moderation tables use.
  Defined in `src/app/features/upload/upload.ts`
- `PATTERNS: Readonly<Record<UiLanguage, string>> = { de: 'dd.MM.yyyy', en: 'MM/dd/yyyy', }` — The date format each language actually expects. Written out rather than left to 'shortDate' , which gives dd.MM.yy in German — a two-digit year on a maintenance record is the one place ambiguity is not worth the four characters it saves. Both patterns are the everyday civil format of their language, not an ISO compromise neither side reads naturally.
  Defined in `src/app/core/i18n/app-date.pipe.ts`
- `PATTERNS_WITH_TIME: Readonly<Record<UiLanguage, string>> = { de: "dd.MM.yyyy, HH:mm 'Uhr'", en: 'MM/dd/yyyy, h:mm a', }` — The same day, with the clock time on it. Added for the protocol viewer's history section, where the day alone is not enough: two corrections on one afternoon are a different story from two a month apart, and a ledger that showed both as "14.08.2026" would hide the sequence a reader is there to reconstruct. The moderation table keeps the day-only format — a column of timestamps is noise in a list somebody is scanning for a title. 24-hour for German and 12-hour with am/pm for English, because that is what each language reads without converting in their head. No seconds: the ledger records an act by a person, and nobody needs to know which second they pressed the button.
  Defined in `src/app/core/i18n/app-date.pipe.ts`
- `POLL_INTERVAL_MS: number = 60_000` — How often the footer asks again, while it is on screen.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/health/health-dot.ts`
- `REJECTION_CODES: unknown = new Set([ 'EMPTY_FILE', 'UNSUPPORTED_TYPE', 'NOT_TEXT', // A correction that is empty or past the size cap. The same rules as an upload, checked by the // same …` — The upload-rejection codes the backend sends with a 400. All three mean the same thing to the person at the keyboard — this file is not something the system can read — so they collapse to one message rather than three that differ only in which technicality was hit. A 400 with any other code stays generic: those are field-level mistakes the form should have prevented.
  Defined in `src/app/core/api/maintenance-api.service.ts`
- `REPO_URL: string = 'https://github.com/Keglev/maintenance-assistant'`
  Defined in `src/app/app.ts`
- `REPO_URL: string = 'https://github.com/Keglev/maintenance-assistant'`
  Defined in `src/app/shared/settings/settings-dialog.ts`
- `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS: number = 5_000` — How long a health request may hang before it counts as down. Without it a backend that accepts the connection and never answers leaves the dot on "checking" forever, which is the one state that tells the reader nothing. Five seconds is far above the endpoint's real cost — it builds no response, it returns a constant — so a slower answer than this already means something is wrong.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/health/health-dot.ts`
- ``routes: Routes = [ // The landing page is what a logged-out visitor gets, at `/` and at `/login` alike: the guard // sends unauthenticated callers to `/login` and `postLogoutRed…``
  Defined in `src/app/app.routes.ts`
- `RULE_LINE: unknown = /^[=-]{3,}$/` — The ===== rule under the WARTUNGSPROTOKOLL / MAINTENANCE PROTOCOL banner.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `SCALES: readonly FontScale[] = ['normal', 'lg', 'xl']`
  Defined in `src/app/core/theme/font-scale.service.ts`
- `SECTION_LINE: unknown = /^(.{1,40}):[ \t]*$/` — A section label alone on its line — the value-less form is what separates it from a meta row.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/protocol/protocol-document.ts`
- `sequence: number = 0` — Makes each instance's title element addressable by aria-labelledby without a collision.
  Defined in `src/app/shared/dialog/dialog.ts`
- `SHOP_FLOOR: [] = ['operator', 'techniker', 'schichtleiter']` — The three roles that work on the shop floor. Admin is deliberately not one of them.
  Defined in `src/app/app.routes.ts`
- `SIGNED_OUT_KEY: string = 'maintenance-assistant.signed-out'` — Marks that this tab signed out deliberately, so the landing page can say so. sessionStorage rather than a query parameter on the redirect: postLogoutRedirectUri is matched against the URIs registered in the realm, and decorating it would risk a Keycloak change this project has decided not to need. It is also the right lifetime — the notice belongs to the tab that signed out, not to every tab on the machine. logOut() clears only its own keys, so this one survives the round trip through Keycloak.
  Defined in `src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts`
- `STORAGE_KEY: string = 'maintenance-assistant.language'` — Where the choice is remembered between visits.
  Defined in `src/app/core/i18n/i18n.service.ts`
- `THEME_STORAGE_KEY: string = 'ma-theme'` — Where the choice is remembered. Shared with public/theme-init.js , which reads the same key before Angular exists — change one and the other stops agreeing.
  Defined in `src/app/core/theme/theme.service.ts`
